Hi Kimberly / Jonas,

We started seeing a small but measurable uptick in downstream tokenization mismatches on our side after pulling the latest client SDK (v2.3) this morning. Traces show that requests to your hosted endpoint sometimes return tokens that don't match the model's expected vocabulary, which causes our post-processing to fallback to older model variants. Impact is intermittent (~0.8% of requests) but affects a subset of production traffic routed through our Canary region.

Can you confirm whether you shipped any compatibility-related changes in the last 24h? We can hold our rollout but want to coordinate a patch/backport if needed. We have logs and a sample request/response we can share.

Thanks,

Hi Maya — thanks for flagging and for the trace. We saw a related anomaly in our telemetry: a rolling deployment yesterday introduced a micro-change to the tokenization wrapper that is benign for most tokens but can cause mismatches for rare Unicode sequences. We're preparing a minimal backport that restores the previous token-normalization path while preserving the larger change.

Plan (high level):
- Build backport to the v2 serving runtime and stage to canary nodes (ETA 60 min).
- Run a 30-minute canary job against Atlas Canary region with your sample trace (we'll need permission to hit your canary endpoint).
- If canary looks good, schedule a 2-hour late-window activation with rolling backfills.

I'll attach the backport diff and the canary checklist shortly. Kimberly / Ben — please coordinate customer comms and the canary verification steps.
